ChIP-Seq Protocol The ChIP-Seq Protocol is separated into four parts: Cell Fixation, Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and Library Preparation, Library Sequencing, and ChIP-Seq Analysis. Note: MYCN ChIP-Seq for Kelly and NGP was performed using a slightly varied procedure and is noted in a separate section. Cell Fixation for ChIP-Seq: Table 3A: Formaldehyde Solution: Manufacturer, Catalog# Final Concentration Per 20 mL Per 10 mL 37% Formaldehyde Sigma, F8775 11% 6 mL 3 mL 5.0 M NaCl Sigma, S5150 0.1 M 0.4 mL 0.2 mL 0.5 EDTA (pH 8.0) Invitrogen, 15575-038 1 mM 40 µL 20 µL 1.0 M HEPES (pH 7.9) Gibco, 15630-080 50 mM 1 mL 0.5 mL Nuclease-free H2O Ambion, AM9937 12.6 mL 6.3 mL Table 3B: Glycine Solution: Reagents Manufacturer, Catalog# Final Concentration Per 20 mL Per 10 mL Glycine (mw 75) Sigma, G7403 2.5 M 3.75 g 1.875 g Nuclease-free H2O Ambion, AM9937 20 mL 10 mL Cell fixation for chromatin immunoprecipitation was performed on adherent cells as described in the Active Motif, Epigenetic Services ChIP Cell Fixation Protocol: 1. Freshly prepare the Formaldehyde solution (Table 3A). 2. Add 1/10th of growth media volume to the existing media in each container of cells (e.g. 1/10 volume of 20 mL of media will have 2 mL added). Gently swirl to mix, and rock the plate for 15 minutes at room temperature. 3. Stop the fixation immediately by adding 1/20th volume of the 2.5M Glycine Solution (Table 3B) to the existing media in each plate (e.g. 22 mL of growth media and Formaldehyde Solution would get 1.1 mL of Glycine Solution). Gently swirl to mix, and then allow to sit at room temperature for 5 minutes. 4. After Glycine incubation, hold the plate at a 45° angle and use a cell scraper to collect cells at the bottom edge of the plate. Use a pipette to transfer the cells to a 50 mL conical tube on ice. Keep samples on ice for the remainder of the procedure.

5. Centrifuge the tube(s) at 800 x g at 4°C for 10 minutes to pellet the cells. 6. Remove and discard the supernatant, and resuspend cells in 10 mL of chilled, sterile 1X PBS by pipetting up and down. If there are multiple tubes (e.g. from multiple plates of the same cell line), the samples can be combined at this step. 7. Centrifuge the tube again as before. Remove and discard the supernatant, then add 10 mL of chilled, sterile 1X PBS to the tube. Add 100 µL of 100 mM PMSF to the tube and pipet up and down to resuspend the cells. 8. Centrifuge the tube at 800 x g at 4°C for 10 minutes. Remove and discard the supernatant. 9. Snap-freeze cells in dry ice, and store at -80°C. 10. Ship cells to Active Motif on dry ice following the instructions listed at on the Sample Submission Form, downloaded from www.activemotif.com/sample-submission. Chromatin Immunoprecipitation (ChIP) and Library Preparation by Active Motif: Table 4: Antibody information and concentration used for ChIP Antibody Manufacturer, Catalog# Amount of Antibody per Immunoprecipitation (IP) Chromatin Concentration per IP N-Myc Active Motif, #61185 6 μl 30 μg c-Myc Santa Cruz N262, #sc-764 20 μl 30 μg H3K4me1 Active Motif, #39297 5 μl 30 μg H3K4me3 Active Motif, #39159 3 μl 30 μg H3K27Ac Active Motif, #39133 4 μg 30 μg HeK27me3 Millipore, #07-449 4 μg 30 μg H3K4me1 Active Motif, #39297 5 μl 30 μg Methods for chromatin immunoprecipitation and library preparation were conducted by Active Motif. In brief: 1. Chromatin was isolated using a lysis buffer and membranes were disrupted with a dounce homogenizer. 2. Lysates were sonicated with Active Motif’s EpiShear probe sonicator ( #53051) and cooled sonication platform (#53080) to an average fragment length 300-500 bp. 3. A portion of the sample was collected as the Input, treated with RNase, proteinase K, and incubated to reverse crosslinking. DNA was collected by ethanol precipitation.

4. Input DNA was resuspended and concentration was quantified by a NanoDrop spectrophotometer. Extrapolation of this concentration to the original chromatin volume allowed for quantitation of the total chromatin yield. 5. Aliquots of fixed chromatin to be used in the immunoprecipitation were precleared with protein A agarose beads (Invitrogen, #15918014). 6. Genomic DNA regions of interest were isolated using specific ChIP antibodies (Table 4). 7. Antibody DNA complexes were isolated using additional beads. 8. The crosslinked DNA, antibody, and bead complexes were washed. 9. The crosslinked DNA was eluted from the beads with an SDS buffer, and subjected to RNase and proteinase K treatment. 10. Reverse crosslinking occurred in an overnight incubation at 65°C, and ChIP DNA was purified with a phenol-chloroform extraction and ethanol precipitation. 11. Illumina sequencing libraries were prepared from the ChIP and Input DNA from the ChIP and Input DNAs using the standard consecutive enzymatic steps of end-polishing, dA-addition, and adaptor ligation using Active Motif’s custom liquid handling robotics pipeline. 12. Samplers were amplified with a 15 cycle PCR amplification and then quantified before being shipped to the Jefferson Cancer Genomics Laboratory at the Kimmel Cancer Center for sequencing. MYCN ChIP-Seq: Kelly and NGP Chromatin immunoprecipitation was performed on adherent cells as described in Bosse et al., 2017. Of note, a different MYCN antibody was used than listed in Bosse et al., 2017. To the existing media, add 415 µL of 37% formaldehyde (final concentration of 0.75%), and rock for 10 minutes at room temperature. 3. Libraries were sequenced as single- end, 50 bp reads on a MiSeq to a depth of ~50 M reads by the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia Nucleic Acid and PCR Core. III. ATAC-Seq Protocol The following ATAC-Seq protocol is adapted from Buenrostro, et. al, 2015. This protocol consists of four parts: Cell Preparation, Transposition Reaction and Purification, PCR Amplification, qPCR, and Library Preparation. Primer 1 and Primer 2 were custom synthesized by Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT), using sequences provided in Buenrostro, et. al, 2015 (Table 7). Note: ATAC-Seq for NB-69 and NGP was performed using a slightly varied procedure and is noted in a separate section. Table 6A: ATAC-Seq Lysis Buffer Reagents Manufacturer, Catalog# Final Concentration Tris-HCl (pH 7.4) Invitrogen, 15567027 10 mM NaCl Sigma, S5150 10 mM MgCl2 Fisher, 7791-18-6 3 mM lgepal CA-630, molecular biology grade Sigma, I8896 0.1% Table 6B: Other Reagents Reagents Manufacturer, Catalog# Final Concentration 1X Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) Gibco, 14190-136 10 mM TDB Illumina, FC-121-1030 (2X reaction buffer from Nextera Kit) 2X TDE1 Illumina, FC-121-30 (Nextera Tn5 Transposase from Nextera Kit) Nuclease-free H2O Ambion, AM9937 NEBNext High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix NEB, M0541 10,000X SYBR Green Invitrogen, S-7563 Cell Preparation: 1. Grow cells in a T-75 flask as described above. 2. Following detachment and pelleting, resuspend cells in 1.0 mL of the appropriate growth media. 3. Triturate until cells are in a homogenous single-cell suspension. 4. Using an automated cell counter, determine the volume which includes 500,000 cells.

5. Aliquot volume for 500,000 cells into sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 500 µL of sterile 1X PBS. 6. Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C. 7. Carefully aspirate off the supernatant, and resuspend cells in 500 µL of sterile 1X PBS. Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C. 8. Carefully aspirate off the supernatant, and then resuspend cells in 500 µ L of cold lysis buffer by gently pipetting up and down. Immediately centrifuge at 500 x g for 10 minutes at 4°C. 9. Carefully remove and discard the supernatant. 10. Resuspend pellet in 50 µL of nuclease free water by gently pipetting up and down, and c ontinue to Transposition Reaction and Purification immediately. Transposition Reaction and Purification: 1. Place cell pellet on ice. 2. Make transposition reaction mix, but combining the following: • 25 µL TD (2X reaction buffer from Nextera Kit) • 2.5 µL TDE1 (Nextera Tn5 Transposase from Nextera Kit) • 17.5 µL nuclease-free water • 5.0 µL of resuspended DNA/protein (from Cell Preparation step 15) 3. Incubate transposition reaction in thermocycler at 37°C for 30-35 minutes. 4. Immediately purify using Qiagen MinElute PCR Purification Kit. Elute transposed DNA in 10.5 µL of elution buffer (Buffer EB from the MinElute Kit consisting of 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8)). 5. Parafilm Eppendorf tube containing purified DNA and store at -20°C if necessary. (Note: This can act as a good stopping point, however these DNA fragments are not PCR amplifiable if melted at this point.) PCR Amplification: Table 7: Primer Sequences used for amplification Primer Name Sequence Concentration Purification

2. Thermal cycle as follows: 1 cycle: 5 min 72°C 30 sec 98°C 5 cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C The five minute extension is critical to allow extension on both ends of the primer after transposition, thereby generating amplifiable fragments. This ensures that downstream quantitative PCR (qPCR) quantitation will not change the complexity of the original library. qPCR: Note: To reduce the GC and size bias in PCR, the appropriate number of PCR cycles (N) is determined using qPCR, allowing us to stop prior to saturation. 1. Keep the samples in the thermocycler following the PCR Amplification reaction and run a qPCR side reaction: • 5 µL of DNA PCR amplified DNA • 2 µL of nuclease free H2O • 1 µL of 6.25 µM Custom Nextera PCR Primer (Ad1) • 1 µL of 6.25 µM Custom Nextera PCR Primer 2 (Ad2.X) • 1 µL 9X SYBR Green I • 5 µL NEBNext High-Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix 2. Cycles on the qPCR instrument are as follows: 1 cycle: 30 sec 98°C 20 cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C 3. To calculate the additional number of cycles needed, plot linear Rn versus cycle and determine the cycle number that corresponds to one-third of the maximum fluorescent intensity.

4. Run the remaining 45 µL PCR reaction to the cycle number determined by qPCR. Cycles are as follows: 1 cycle: 30 sec 98°C N cycles: 10 sec 98°C 30 sec 63°C 1 min 72°C 6. Purify the amplified library using Qiagen MinElute PCR Purification Kit. Elute purified library in 20 µL of elution buffer (Buffer EB from the MinElute Kit consisting of 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8)). Make sure that the column is dry prior to adding elution buffer to avoid ethanol contamination of final library. (Note: Sample can be stored at -20°C at this point.) 7. Purify amplified library using AMPure XP beads at a 1.8x ratio to get rid of adapter dimer, using 80% ethanol for the wash steps. Elute in 50 µL of nuclease free H2O. (Note: Sample can be parafilmed and stored at -20°C at this point, if needed.) 8. Concentration of the DNA eluted from the column should be about 30 nM. Library Preparation 1. Assess the quality of purified libraries using a Bioanalyzer High-Sensitivity DNA Analysis kit (Agilent). 2. If large, predominant peak exists around 1000 bp, remove with SPRI beads. • First, with a new vial of SPRI beads, perform size selection with various ratios to ensure large peak is removed. For example, 0.4X, 0.45X, 0.5X. Choose the ratio that removes 1000 bp fragments, but leaves 800 bp fragments. • Elute in 20 µL of nuclease-free water. Note: Samples can be parafilmed and stored at -20°C at this point. 3. Libraries were sequenced by Beijing Genomics International at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. Sequencing for ATAC-Seq by Beijing Genomics International (BGI):

Methods for sequencing were conducted by Beijing Genomics International at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. In brief: 1. Samples were quality control tested using an Agilent High Sensitivity Screen Tape to confirm average fragment sizes were ~180, 380, 580, 780, 980 bp. 2. The concentration of each library was measured using a High Sensitivity Qubit Quantification kit, to ensure they were ≥ 5.5 nM. 3. Samples were normalized and libraries were pooled together in equal amounts. 4. Samples were sequenced as paired-end, 100 bp to an average depth of 80M reads on a HiSeq 2500. ATAC-Seq for NB-69 and NGP via Active Motif: 1. Grow cells in a T-75 cm2 flask as described above. 2. Following detachment and pelleting, resuspend cells in 1.0 mL of the appropriate growth media. 3. Triturate until cells are in a homogenous single-cell suspension. 4. Using an automated cell counter, determine the volume which includes 100,000 cells. 5. Aliquot volume for 100,000 cells into a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 500 µL of sterile 1X PBS. 6. Centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C. 7. Carefully aspirate off the supernatant, and resuspend cells in 500 µL of growth media plus 5% DMSO and transfer to a 1.7 mL microfuge tube on ice. 8. Freeze the cells at a slow cooling to minimize cell lysis. A Mr. Frosty (Thermo Scientific, 5100-0001) container was used in this preparation. 11. Ship samples on dry ice to Active Motif (1914 Palomar Oaks Way, Ste 150, Carlsbad, CA 92008) following the instructions listed at on the Sample Submission Form, downloaded from www.activemotif.com/sample-submission. 12. Samples were prepared and sequenced following Active Motif’s ATAC-Seq proprietary protocol. If brief: a. Cells were thawed in a 37oC water bath, pelleted, washed with cold PBS, and tagmented as previously described (Buenrostro et al. 2013), with some modifications based on (Corces et al. 2017).

b. Cell pellets were resuspended in lysis buffer, pelleted, and tagmented using the enzyme buffer provided in the Nextera Library Prep Kit (Illumina). c. Tagmented DNA was then purified using the MinElute PCR purification kit (Qiagen), amplified with 10 cycles of PCR, and purified using Agencourt AMPure SPRI beads (Beckman Coulter). d. The resulting material was quantified using the KAPA Library Quantification Kit for Illumina platforms (KAPA Biosystems) and sequenced with PE42 sequencing on the NextSeq 500 sequencer (Illumina). ATAC-Seq Analysis Samples were quality-controlled and trimmed as described in Chip-Seq Analysis. FASTQ files were aligned using bwa aln for BGI samples (100 bp reads) and bwa mem for Active Motif samples (42 bp reads). Reads with mapping quality < 10 were discarded. Biological duplicate BAMs were merged using Picard tools. Broad peaks were called using --extsize 200 and --shift 100. Peaks were called significant using a q-value (minimum False Discovery Rate) cut off of 0.05. Results were returned in units of signal per million reads to get normalized peak values. Finally, repetitive centromeric, telomeric and satellite regions known to have low sequencing confidence were removed using the blacklisted regions defined by UCSC. steps.title: Thaw frozen cells
steps.instruction: Float cryovials in a 37 °C water bath for 2–3 minutes until cells are thawed.

steps.title: Pellet cells and remove freezing media
steps.instruction: Add thawed cells to a 15 mL tube containing 5 mL of the appropriate growth medium, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add cells to 15 mL tube with 5 mL appropriate growth media (see Table 2).
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 300 × g for 5 min at RT.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in fresh medium
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant to discard DMSO‑containing freezing media and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL fresh growth medium.

steps.title: Seed cells in T‑75 flask and incubate
steps.instruction: Transfer the 1 mL cell suspension to a T‑75 flask containing 10 mL growth medium and incubate at 37 °C with 5.0 % CO₂.

steps.title: Wash confluent cells with PBS
steps.instruction: When cultures reach ~70–80 % confluence, aspirate the medium, gently wash cells with sterile 1X PBS, and aspirate off the PBS.

steps.title: Detach cells with appropriate solution
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of the detachment solution listed for the cell line (Table 2), incubate at room temperature or 37 °C until cells detach (~2–5 min), and confirm detachment visually or with a microscope.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at RT or 37 °C until cells are detached (~2–5 min).
Confirm detachment by eye or microscope.

steps.title: Collect detached cells with growth medium
steps.instruction: Tilt the plate to a 45° angle and rinse the cells with at least 4 mL of the appropriate growth medium to collect them.

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend for plating
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL conical tube and centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Collect cells in 15 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Plate cells in 150 mm dish and grow
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL appropriate growth medium, and transfer to a 150 mm dish containing 19 mL growth medium. Grow to ~70–80 % confluence.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 1 mL growth medium.
Transfer to 150 mm dish with 19 mL growth medium.

steps.title: Prepare cells for downstream assays
steps.instruction: When cultures reach ~70–80 % confluence again, remove dishes from the incubator and pellet or cross‑link cells as required for ChIP‑Seq or ATAC‑Seq.

steps.title: Assess library fragment length
steps.instruction: Test each library on an Agilent High Sensitivity Screen Tape to determine average fragment length.

steps.title: Quantify library concentration and dilute
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration with a High Sensitivity Qubit kit and dilute each library to ≤4 nM for loading.

steps.title: Normalize and pool libraries equally
steps.instruction: Normalize all libraries to the same nanomolar concentration and pool them together in equal volumes.

steps.title: Dilute pooled library to final concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the pooled library to 1.51 pM in Low‑EDTA TE Buffer.

steps.title: Sequence libraries on NextSeq 500
steps.instruction: Sequence the libraries as single‑end 70 bp reads to an average depth of ~30 million reads on a NextSeq 500 instrument.

steps.title: Amplify transposed DNA for ATAC‑Seq
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL PCR tube combine 10 µL transposed DNA, 10 µL nuclease‑free H₂O, 2.5 µL 25 µM PCR Primer 1 (Ad1), 2.5 µL 25 µM barcoded PCR Primer 2 (Ad2.X), and 25 µL NEBNext High‑Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix; then proceed with PCR cycling as per protocol.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.5 µL 25 µM barcoded PCR Primer 2 (Ad2.X).
Add 25 µL NEBNext High‑Fidelity 2X PCR Master Mix.
